0.0.n: A standard greeting suitable for introducing a video.

0.2.n: Comes directly before a noun to identify something close to the speaker.

0.3.n: The first 動画 identifies the video being introduced.

0.4.n: Marks this video as the topic of the sentence.

0.5.n: A brand name, forming part of the product name Amazfit Bip U.

0.7.n: Part of the product name Amazfit Bip U.

0.9.n: The model designation in the product name Amazfit Bip U.

0.10.n: Links the product name to its unboxing review.

0.11.n: A noun referring to opening the product's packaging.

0.12.n: A borrowed word combined with 開封 to describe the video's content.

0.13.n: The second 動画 names the type of content: an unboxing review video.

0.14.n: Marks what the video is presented as before なります.

0.15.n: Polite form of なる; here it formally introduces the video's nature rather than describing an actual change.

1.0.n: A brand name within the full product name Amazfit Bip U.

1.2.n: Part of the product name Amazfit Bip U.

1.4.n: The model designation in the product name Amazfit Bip U.

1.5.n: Marks the smartwatch as the topic for the comments that follow.

1.6.n: A borrowed noun modifying 持続時間 to specify battery life.

1.7.n: Combines with 時間 to form 持続時間, the length of time something lasts.

1.8.n: Together with バッテリー持続, refers to how long the battery lasts.

1.9.n: Identifies battery life as what has decreased.

1.10.n: Emphasizes the extent of the decrease.

1.11.n: Connecting form of 減る, linking the decrease to the next statement without ending the sentence.

1.13.n: Refers to people's overall opinion of the product.

1.14.n: Marks reputation as the thing described as not good.

1.15.n: 良い becomes 良くない in the negative; です adds politeness.

1.16.n: Connects this negative assessment to the contrasting point that follows.

2.0.n: Points to the video the viewer is currently watching.

2.1.n: Names what the viewer will finish watching.

2.2.n: Marks the video as the object of 見終わった.

2.3.n: 見る combines with 終わる; the past form marks watching as completed before the stated time.

2.4.n: Follows a describing phrase to express when something happens.

2.5.n: Marks the time when the viewer is expected to have this opinion.

2.6.n: Adds emphasis to the time phrase, suggesting that things will be different by then.

2.8.n: Casually indicates a fairly high degree, modifying いい.

2.9.n: An everyday form of 良い, describing the smartwatch positively.

2.10.n: A borrowed noun naming the type of device being reviewed.

2.11.n: Connects the noun スマートウォッチ to explanatory ん.

2.12.n: Short for の; adds an explanatory tone to the assessment.

2.13.n: Casual contraction of では; pairs with ない to form a negative expression.

2.14.n: With じゃ and か, helps frame a tentative positive judgment rather than a direct denial.

2.15.n: Completes んじゃないか, presenting the positive assessment as a tentative thought.

2.16.n: Marks the preceding assessment as the content of 思う.

2.17.n: The unstated person doing the thinking is the viewer.

2.18.n: Expresses the speaker's confident expectation, not an obligation.

2.19.n: Connects はず to ので to introduce a reason.

2.20.n: Gives the expected change of opinion as the reason for the request in the next line.

3.0.n: A noun naming the action being considered.

3.1.n: Marks 購入 as what people are considering.

3.2.n: 検討する in the ている form describes ongoing consideration and modifies 人.

3.3.n: The preceding phrase identifies these people as those considering a purchase.

3.4.n: Marks people considering a purchase as the audience addressed by the request.

3.5.n: Adds warm encouragement to the request.

3.6.n: Refers to the final part of the video.

3.7.n: Marks the end as the point up to which viewers should watch.

3.8.n: A respectful expression for looking or watching, used here in ご覧ください.

3.9.n: Completes ご覧ください, making a polite, respectful request to watch.

4.0.n: Signals a transition from the introduction to the main content.

4.1.n: Polite invitation form of 行く; here it means moving on with the video, not physically going somewhere.

0.lit: Hello. This video, as for, is an Amazfit Bip U unboxing review video.
0.tip: となります is a formal presentation-style way to say what something is here.

1.lit: Amazfit Bip U, as for, battery lasting time has decreased considerably, and reputation is not good, but…
1.tip: 減り connects to another statement, while the final が signals a contrast still to come.

2.lit: Because, when you have finished watching this video, you should think that it is perhaps a pretty good smartwatch…
2.tip: んじゃないかと思う softens a positive opinion into something like I think it might actually be good.

3.lit: People considering a purchase, as for, by all means please watch until the end.
3.tip: ご覧ください is a respectful way to ask someone to watch or look.

4.tip: 行きましょう can invite the audience to get started, without implying physical movement.
